label: be — present affirmative, full forms
form: I am / you are / he-she-it is / we-you-they are
meaning: identifies, describes and locates the subject
use: saying who you are, where you are, how you are

explanation.en: English needs a verb in every sentence. To say who or what something is, use am, is or are.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tilida har bir gapda fe'l bo'lishi shart. Kim yoki nima ekanini aytish uchun am, is, are ishlatiladi.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida hozirgi zamonda bog'lama tushib qoladi ('Men talaba') — ingliz tilida esa 'am/is/are' majburiy.
l1_notes.ru: В русском связка в настоящем времени опускается ('Я студент') — в английском be обязателен.

can_do: I can say who I am and where I am from.

label: be — contracted forms
form: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're
use: normal spoken and informal written English

explanation.en: In speech we almost always join the pronoun and be: I am becomes I'm.
explanation.uz: Nutqda olmosh va 'be' deyarli doim qo'shilib aytiladi: I am → I'm.

l1_notes.uz: Qisqartma shakl yozuvda ham, nutqda ham normal — lekin qisqa javobda ishlatilmaydi: 'Yes, I am.'

can_do: I can use short forms like I'm and she's.

label: be — present negative
form: I'm not / you aren't (you're not) / he isn't (he's not)
use: correcting, denying, saying what is not true

explanation.en: Put not after am, is or are. Both he isn't and he's not are correct.
explanation.uz: 'not' so'zi am/is/are dan keyin qo'yiladi. 'he isn't' ham, 'he's not' ham to'g'ri.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekcha inkor fe'lga '-ma' qo'shimchasi bilan yasaladi; ingliz tilida esa alohida 'not' so'zi kerak.
l1_notes.ru: Русское 'не' ставится перед словом; английское not ставится ПОСЛЕ be.

can_do: I can say what is not true about me or others.

label: be — yes/no questions and short answers
form: Am I…? Are you…? Is he…? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
use: checking facts about people and things

explanation.en: Put am, is or are before the subject. In short answers, never use a short form after Yes.
explanation.uz: am/is/are ni egadan oldin qo'ying. Qisqa javobda 'Yes' dan keyin qisqartma ishlatilmaydi.

positive_example: Are you a student? — Yes, I am.
negative_example: You are a student? — Yes, I'm.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida savol '-mi' yuklamasi bilan yasaladi, so'z tartibi o'zgarmaydi. Ingliz tilida esa fe'l oldinga chiqadi (inversiya).
l1_notes.ru: В русском вопрос делается интонацией; в английском нужен порядок слов be + подлежащее.

can_do: I can ask yes/no questions and answer them correctly.

label: be — wh-questions
form: What / Where / Who / How + am, is, are + subject

explanation.en: Question word first, then am/is/are, then the subject.
explanation.uz: Avval so'roq so'zi, keyin am/is/are, keyin ega.

known_errors: *What is your name? — My name Aziz.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada so'roq so'zi gap o'rtasida ham kelishi mumkin; ingliz tilida esa doim boshida va undan keyin inversiya bo'ladi.

can_do: I can ask for someone's name, country and how they are.

label: be — past (was / were)
form: I/he/she/it was; you/we/they were; wasn't, weren't
meaning: identity, state or location in past time
use: talking about where you were and how things were

explanation.en: Was and were are the past of be. Was goes with I, he, she, it. Were goes with you, we, they.
explanation.uz: was va were — 'be' fe'lining o'tgan zamoni. was: I, he, she, it bilan. were: you, we, they bilan.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada 'edi' barcha shaxslar uchun bir xil; ingliz tilida was/were farqlanadi.

can_do: I can say where I was and how I felt.

label: there is / there are
form: There is + singular; There are + plural; There isn't / There aren't; Is there…? Are there…?
use: describing a room, a town, a picture

explanation.en: Use there is / there are to say that something exists. There is not the same as it is.
explanation.uz: Biror narsaning borligini aytish uchun there is / there are ishlatiladi. Bu 'it is' bilan bir xil emas.

positive_example: There are two windows in my room.
negative_example: In my room have two windows.
known_errors: *In the table there are a lamp.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada 'bor/yo'q' ishlatiladi va ega oldinga chiqadi: 'Xonamda ikkita deraza bor'. Ingliz tilida gap doim 'There' bilan boshlanadi.
l1_notes.ru: Русское 'есть' — здесь нужен формальный подлежащий there.

can_do: I can describe what is in a room or a place.

label: there was / there were
form: There was + singular; There were + plural
use: describing a past place or situation

explanation.en: The past of there is / there are.
explanation.uz: there is / there are ning o'tgan zamon shakli.

positive_example: There were a lot of people at the party.
negative_example: There was a lot of people at the party.

l1_notes.uz: 'bor edi' — lekin ingliz tilida son bo'yicha was/were tanlanadi.

can_do: I can describe a place or event in the past.

label: have got / has got and have / has for possession
form: I have got / I've got; he has got / he's got; I have / he has
use: talking about family, things you own, appearance

explanation.en: Both have and have got mean the same. Have got is more common in Britain, have in America.
explanation.uz: have va have got bir xil ma'noni beradi. Britaniyada have got, Amerikada have ko'proq ishlatiladi.

positive_example: I have two brothers. / I've got two brothers.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada egalik '-im/-ing + bor' bilan ifodalanadi ('mening akam bor'); ingliz tilida esa 'have' fe'li kerak.
l1_notes.ru: Русское 'у меня есть' калькируется как *At me is — это ошибка.

can_do: I can say what I have and who is in my family.

label: have got / have — negatives and questions
form: Have you got…? / Do you have…? — I haven't got / I don't have

explanation.en: Have got makes questions with have. Have alone makes questions with do.
explanation.uz: 'have got' savolini 'have' bilan, oddiy 'have' savolini esa 'do' bilan yasaymiz.

positive_example: Do you have a pen? / Have you got a pen?

l1_notes.uz: Ikki tizimni aralashtirmang: 'have got' → have bilan; 'have' → do bilan.

can_do: I can ask people what they have.

label: possessive 's and s'
form: noun + 's (singular); noun + s' (regular plural); of + noun for things

explanation.en: Add 's to a person: my sister's bag. For things we usually use of: the door of the car.
explanation.uz: Odamga 's qo'shiladi: my sister's bag. Jonsiz narsalarda odatda 'of' ishlatiladi: the door of the car.

negative_example: This is the bag of my sister.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada qaratqich kelishigi ('-ning') va egalik qo'shimchasi ikkalasi ham bor; ingliz tilida faqat 's.

can_do: I can say who something belongs to.

label: possessive adjectives
form: my, your, his, her, its, our, their + noun

explanation.en: Possessive adjectives never change for singular or plural: my book, my books.
explanation.uz: Egalik sifatlari birlik va ko'plikda o'zgarmaydi: my book, my books.

negative_example: His name is Dilnoza. (for a woman)

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada 'u' jinsni ko'rsatmaydi, shuning uchun his/her chalkashtiriladi — bu eng ko'p uchraydigan xato. Har doim shaxsning jinsini o'ylab tanlang.

can_do: I can say whose something is, using his and her correctly.

label: possessive pronouns
form: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs

explanation.en: Use these instead of repeating the noun: This is my bag → This bag is mine.
explanation.uz: Otni takrorlamaslik uchun ishlatiladi: This is my bag → This bag is mine.

l1_notes.uz: 'hers' va 'his' farqiga e'tibor bering; 'her' sifat, 'hers' olmosh.

can_do: I can answer the question Whose is this?

label: whose
form: Whose + noun + be…? / Whose is this?

explanation.en: Whose asks about the owner. Do not confuse it with who's (= who is).
explanation.uz: 'Whose' egasini so'raydi. 'who's' (= who is) bilan chalkashtirmang.

l1_notes.uz: 'kimning' — lekin yozuvda who's bilan adashmang.

can_do: I can ask who something belongs to.

label: present simple — affirmative (I/you/we/they)
form: subject + base verb
use: describing your daily life and general truths

explanation.en: Use the present simple for things that happen regularly or are always true.
explanation.uz: Muntazam takrorlanadigan yoki doim to'g'ri bo'lgan ishlar uchun ishlatiladi.

negative_example: I am work in a hospital.
known_errors: *Every day I am go to school.

l1_notes.uz: 'be' fe'lini asosiy fe'l bilan birga ishlatmang: *I am work — noto'g'ri.

can_do: I can describe my daily routine.

label: present simple — third person -s
form: he/she/it + verb + -s / -es / -ies
use: talking about one other person or thing

explanation.en: Add -s to the verb after he, she or it. After -ch, -sh, -s, -x, -o add -es. After consonant + y, change y to -ies.
explanation.uz: he, she, it dan keyin fe'lga -s qo'shiladi. -ch, -sh, -s, -x, -o dan keyin -es. Undosh + y bo'lsa, y → -ies.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada fe'l shaxs bo'yicha o'zgaradi, lekin uchinchi shaxs '-s' ingliz tilida oxirgi o'zlashtiriladigan qo'shimchalardan biri — sabr qiling, u sekin mustahkamlanadi.

can_do: I can talk about what another person does every day.

label: present simple — negative with don't / doesn't
form: don't / doesn't + base verb
use: saying what you do not do

explanation.en: Use don't with I, you, we, they and doesn't with he, she, it. After doesn't the verb has no -s.
explanation.uz: I, you, we, they bilan don't; he, she, it bilan doesn't. doesn't dan keyin fe'lga -s QO'SHILMAYDI.

l1_notes.uz: Ingliz tilida inkorni 'do' yordamchi fe'li ko'taradi, shuning uchun asosiy fe'l asl shaklda qoladi.

can_do: I can say what I and other people do not do.

label: present simple — yes/no questions with do / does
form: Do / Does + subject + base verb? — Yes, I do. / No, he doesn't.

explanation.en: Start with Do or Does. The main verb has no -s. Answer with do or does, not with the main verb.
explanation.uz: Do yoki Does bilan boshlang. Asosiy fe'lga -s qo'shilmaydi. Javobda ham do/does ishlatiladi.

positive_example: Does she speak English? — Yes, she does.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada savol '-mi' bilan yasaladi va yordamchi fe'l kerak emas; ingliz tilida 'do/does' majburiy.

can_do: I can ask someone about their habits and answer.

label: present simple — wh-questions with do / does
form: Wh- + do / does + subject + base verb?
meaning: asks for specific information about habits
use: asking where someone lives, what they do

explanation.en: Question word, then do or does, then the subject, then the base verb.
explanation.uz: So'roq so'zi → do/does → ega → fe'lning asl shakli.

l1_notes.uz: So'roq so'zidan keyin ham do/does tushib qolmasligi kerak.

can_do: I can ask where someone lives and what they do.

label: subject questions without do
form: Who / What + verb (+ -s) …?
meaning: asks about the doer of the action

explanation.en: When who or what is the subject, do not use do or does: Who lives here?
explanation.uz: 'who' yoki 'what' ega bo'lsa, do/does ishlatilmaydi: Who lives here?

negative_example: Who does live in this house?

l1_notes.uz: Bu qoida o'zbek tilida ekvivalenti yo'q — ega savoli va to'ldiruvchi savolini farqlashni o'rganish kerak.

can_do: I can ask who does something.

label: adverbs of frequency
form: always, usually, often, sometimes, never — before the main verb, after be

explanation.en: Frequency adverbs go BEFORE the main verb but AFTER the verb be.
explanation.uz: Takrorlanish ravishlari asosiy fe'ldan OLDIN, lekin 'be' fe'lidan KEYIN keladi.

positive_example: I always get up at seven. / She is never late.
negative_example: I get up always at seven.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada ravish erkin joylashadi; ingliz tilida joyi qat'iy. Shuningdek 'never' o'zi inkor — 'don't never' noto'g'ri.

can_do: I can say how often I do things.

label: frequency expressions
form: every day, once a week, twice a month, three times a year

explanation.en: Once and twice are special. From three, use the number + times.
explanation.uz: 'once' va 'twice' maxsus shakllar. Uchdan boshlab: son + times.

positive_example: I go to the gym three times a week.
negative_example: I go to the gym three time in week.
known_errors: *two times a week (acceptable but twice is better)

l1_notes.uz: 'haftasiga uch marta' → 'three times a week' ('a' = 'per').

can_do: I can say exactly how often I do something.

label: present continuous — form
form: am / is / are + verb-ing

explanation.en: Use be + verb-ing. Spelling: run → running, make → making, lie → lying.
explanation.uz: be + fe'l-ing. Imlo: run → running, make → making, lie → lying.

l1_notes.uz: 'be' tushib qolmasligi kerak — bu eng ko'p uchraydigan xato.

can_do: I can say what is happening right now.

label: present continuous — actions happening now
form: be + -ing with now, at the moment, right now, look!, listen!
meaning: in progress at the moment of speaking
use: describing a picture or a live scene

explanation.en: Use it for what is happening at this moment.
explanation.uz: Aynan shu daqiqada sodir bo'layotgan ish uchun ishlatiladi.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchadagi '-yapti' shakliga yaqin — bu yaxshi tayanch nuqta.

can_do: I can describe what people are doing in a picture.

label: present continuous — temporary situations
form: be + -ing with these days, this week, this year, at the moment
meaning: true around now but not permanent
use: describing temporary jobs, studies, living arrangements

explanation.en: Use it for something temporary, even if it is not happening this second.
explanation.uz: Vaqtinchalik holat uchun — hozir shu daqiqada bo'lmasa ham.

positive_example: I'm living with my cousin this month.
negative_example: I live with my cousin this month only.
known_errors: *I work in a café this summer. (if temporary)
*These days I study a lot. (continuous is better)

l1_notes.uz: Doimiy va vaqtinchalik farqi o'zbek tilida grammatik emas — bu farqni alohida o'rganish kerak.

can_do: I can talk about temporary situations in my life.

label: present simple vs present continuous
form: contrast of the two forms

explanation.en: Simple = always, usually, every day. Continuous = now, at the moment, this week.
explanation.uz: Simple = doim, odatda, har kuni. Continuous = hozir, shu paytda, shu hafta.

positive_example: I usually walk to work, but today I'm taking the bus.
negative_example: I usually am walking to work.

l1_notes.uz: Vaqt so'zlariga qarang: 'every day' → simple; 'now' → continuous.

can_do: I can choose correctly between I work and I'm working.

label: state verbs
form: know, like, want, need, understand, believe, belong, own, seem, hate, love, prefer, remember, forget, mean, cost, contain
use: these verbs are normally not used in the continuous

explanation.en: Some verbs describe states, not actions. We do not usually use them with -ing.
explanation.uz: Ba'zi fe'llar harakatni emas, holatni bildiradi. Ular odatda -ing bilan ishlatilmaydi.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada bu fe'llarni davomiy shaklda ishlatish mumkin, ingliz tilida esa yo'q.

can_do: I can avoid the -ing form with verbs like know and want.

label: be past in narrative
form: was / were in a sequence of past sentences
use: telling where you were and what it was like

explanation.en: Use was and were to set the scene of a past story.
explanation.uz: O'tmishdagi vaziyatni tasvirlash uchun was/were ishlatiladi.

positive_example: It was Sunday. We were at my grandmother's house.
negative_example: It is Sunday. We are at my grandmother's house. (in a past story)

l1_notes.uz: Hikoyada zamon o'zgarmasligi kerak — boshdan oxirigacha o'tgan zamon.

can_do: I can describe a past scene.

label: past simple — regular verbs
form: verb + -ed; spelling: stop → stopped, study → studied, like → liked

explanation.en: Add -ed. The ending sounds three ways: /t/ after voiceless sounds, /d/ after voiced, /ɪd/ after t or d.
explanation.uz: -ed qo'shiladi. Uch xil talaffuz: jarangsizdan keyin /t/, jaranglidan keyin /d/, t yoki d dan keyin /ɪd/.

positive_example: I watched a film last night.
negative_example: I watch a film last night.

l1_notes.uz: -ed ning talaffuzi imlodan farq qiladi: 'worked' = /wɝkt/, 'wanted' = /ˈwɑntɪd/.

can_do: I can say what I did yesterday.

label: past simple — irregular verbs, set 1
form: was/were, had, did, went, said, got, made, knew, saw, came, took, thought, gave, found, told, became, left, felt, put, brought, began, kept, held, wrote, stood, heard, let, meant, set, met
use: talking about the past with the most frequent verbs

explanation.en: These 30 verbs do not take -ed. They must be learned one by one — but they are the ones you need most.
explanation.uz: Bu 30 ta fe'l -ed olmaydi. Ularni yodlash kerak — lekin aynan ular eng ko'p kerak bo'ladi.

positive_example: I went to Bukhara last summer.
negative_example: I goed to Bukhara last summer.

l1_notes.uz: Naqsh bo'yicha guruhlab o'rganing — alifbo tartibida emas.

can_do: I can use the 30 most common past verbs.

label: past simple — negative
form: didn't + base verb
use: saying what you did not do

explanation.en: Use didn't with the base verb — never with the past form.
explanation.uz: didn't dan keyin fe'lning ASL shakli keladi, o'tgan zamon shakli emas.

positive_example: I didn't go to work yesterday.
negative_example: I didn't went to work yesterday.

l1_notes.uz: O'tgan zamon belgisi 'did' ga o'tadi, shuning uchun asosiy fe'l asl shaklda qoladi.

can_do: I can say what I did not do.

label: past simple — questions and short answers
form: Did + subject + base verb? — Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
use: asking about someone's weekend, holiday, day

explanation.en: Did + subject + base verb. The main verb never changes.
explanation.uz: Did + ega + fe'lning asl shakli. Asosiy fe'l o'zgarmaydi.

positive_example: Did you see the film? — Yes, I did.

l1_notes.uz: Savolda ham 'did' o'tgan zamonni ko'taradi.

can_do: I can ask someone about their weekend.

label: past time expressions
form: yesterday, last night/week/year, two days ago, in 2019, when I was a child
meaning: locates an action in past time

explanation.en: Ago counts back from now: two days ago. Last has no the: last week, not the last week.
explanation.uz: 'ago' hozirdan orqaga sanaydi: two days ago. 'last' bilan 'the' ishlatilmaydi.

positive_example: I moved here three years ago.
negative_example: I moved here before three years.

l1_notes.uz: 'uch yil oldin' → 'three years ago' (so'z tartibi teskari).
l1_notes.ru: 'три года назад' → three years ago, не *before three years.

can_do: I can say exactly when something happened.

label: be going to — plans and intentions
form: am / is / are going to + base verb

explanation.en: Use be going to for something you have already decided to do.
explanation.uz: Allaqachon qaror qilingan ish uchun 'be going to' ishlatiladi.

known_errors: *I will go to study medicine. (for a firm plan)

l1_notes.uz: 'be' tushib qolmasin. Nutqda 'going to' ko'pincha /ˈɡʌnə/ deb aytiladi.

can_do: I can talk about my plans.

label: be going to — predictions from evidence
form: be going to + base verb
meaning: a prediction based on what you can see now

explanation.en: Use going to when you can see it coming: Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
explanation.uz: Hozirgi dalilga asoslangan bashorat: Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.

positive_example: Look out! You're going to fall.
known_errors: *Look at the clouds, it will rain.

l1_notes.uz: Ko'rinib turgan dalil bo'lsa — going to; shunchaki fikr bo'lsa — will (A2 da).

can_do: I can predict what is about to happen.

label: present continuous for fixed arrangements
form: be + -ing with a future time expression
meaning: an arrangement already fixed with another person

explanation.en: Use the present continuous for arrangements with a time and place already fixed.
explanation.uz: Vaqti va joyi allaqachon kelishilgan rejalar uchun present continuous ishlatiladi.

positive_example: I'm meeting Aziz at six tomorrow.
negative_example: I meet Aziz at six tomorrow.
known_errors: *I will meet him at six. (for a fixed arrangement)

l1_notes.uz: Kelasi zamon ma'nosida hozirgi davomiy zamon ishlatilishi o'zbek tilida g'alati tuyuladi — kalendardagi yozuv deb tasavvur qiling.

can_do: I can talk about my arrangements for tomorrow.

label: can / can't — ability
form: can / can't + base verb (no to, no -s)

explanation.en: Can never changes and is never followed by to.
explanation.uz: 'can' hech qachon o'zgarmaydi va undan keyin 'to' kelmaydi.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada '-a olmoq' qo'shimchasi — ingliz tilida esa alohida modal fe'l, undan keyin 'to' YO'Q.
l1_notes.ru: 'мочь + инфинитив' — но в английском без to.

can_do: I can say what I can and can't do.

label: can / can't — permission and requests
form: Can I…? Can you…?

explanation.en: Can I…? asks permission. Can you…? asks someone to do something.
explanation.uz: Can I…? — ruxsat so'rash. Can you…? — kimdandir biror ish so'rash.

negative_example: I can open the window? (as a request)

l1_notes.uz: So'rovda intonatsiya ko'tariladi; buyruq ohangi qo'pol eshitiladi.

can_do: I can ask for permission and for help.

label: could — polite request (chunk)
form: Could I…? Could you…?
meaning: a more polite version of can
use: requests to strangers, in shops, at work

explanation.en: Could is more polite than can. Learn it as a phrase for now.
explanation.uz: 'could' — 'can' ga qaraganda muloyimroq. Hozircha tayyor ibora sifatida yodlang.

negative_example: Could you to help me, please?
known_errors: *Can you give me a coffee. (too direct with a stranger)

l1_notes.uz: Ingliz tilida notanish odamga murojaat qilganda bilvosita shakl kutiladi; to'g'ridan-to'g'ri buyruq qo'pol eshitiladi.

can_do: I can make a polite request.

label: would like (chunk)
form: I'd like + noun / to + verb; Would you like…?

explanation.en: I'd like is a polite I want. Would you like…? offers something.
explanation.uz: 'I'd like' — 'I want' ning muloyim shakli. 'Would you like…?' — taklif qilish.

known_errors: *I would like a coffee? (as a statement)
*Do you like a coffee? (as an offer)

l1_notes.uz: 'I want' juda to'g'ridan-to'g'ri — kafeda va do'konda 'I'd like' ishlating.
l1_notes.ru: 'Я хочу' → в английском лучше I'd like.

can_do: I can order politely in a café or shop.

label: must / mustn't
form: must / mustn't + base verb

explanation.en: Must = it is necessary. Mustn't = it is forbidden — not the opposite of must.
explanation.uz: must = shart. mustn't = TAQIQLANGAN — 'shart emas' degani EMAS.

known_errors: *You mustn't come if you don't want. (meaning: don't have to)

l1_notes.uz: 'mustn't' = taqiq, 'don't have to' = shart emas. Bu ikkisi butunlay boshqa ma'no.

can_do: I can understand and give rules.

label: have to / don't have to
form: have to / has to / don't have to / doesn't have to + base verb

explanation.en: Have to = someone else requires it. Don't have to = it is not necessary (you can if you want).
explanation.uz: have to = tashqi majburiyat. don't have to = shart emas (xohlasang qilishing mumkin).

positive_example: I don't have to work on Sundays.
negative_example: I mustn't work on Sundays. (meaning: it isn't necessary)

l1_notes.uz: 'have to' oddiy fe'l — savol va inkorda do/does kerak.

can_do: I can say what I have to do and what is not necessary.

label: should / shouldn't — advice
form: should / shouldn't + base verb

explanation.en: Should gives advice. It is softer than must.
explanation.uz: 'should' maslahat beradi. U 'must' ga qaraganda yumshoqroq.

negative_example: You should to see a doctor.
known_errors: *You must rest. (as friendly advice — too strong)

l1_notes.uz: Do'stona maslahatda 'must' emas, 'should' ishlating — 'must' buyruqdek eshitiladi.

can_do: I can give simple advice.

label: let's + base verb
form: Let's + base verb / Let's not + base verb

explanation.en: Let's = let us. Use the base verb after it.
explanation.uz: Let's = let us. Undan keyin fe'lning asl shakli keladi.

negative_example: Let's to go to the park.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchadagi '-aylik' shakliga to'g'ri keladi.

can_do: I can suggest doing something together.

label: imperative — affirmative
form: base verb (no subject)

explanation.en: Use the base verb with no subject: Sit down. Turn left.
explanation.uz: Egasiz fe'lning asl shakli: Sit down. Turn left.

negative_example: You turn left at the bank. (as an instruction)

l1_notes.uz: Buyruq shakli o'zbekchada ham egasiz — bu oson. Lekin so'rov uchun buyruq qo'pol: 'please' yoki 'could you' qo'shing.

can_do: I can give simple instructions and directions.

label: imperative — negative
form: Don't + base verb

explanation.en: Put Don't before the verb: Don't worry.
explanation.uz: Fe'l oldiga Don't qo'yiladi: Don't worry.

known_errors: *No smoking here. (as an imperative to a person)

l1_notes.uz: '-ma' qo'shimchasi o'rniga alohida 'Don't' so'zi.

can_do: I can tell someone not to do something.

label: regular plurals
form: -s / -es / -ies; pronounced /s/, /z/ or /ɪz/

explanation.en: Add -s. After -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o add -es. After consonant + y, change to -ies.
explanation.uz: -s qo'shiladi. -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o dan keyin -es. Undosh + y bo'lsa -ies.

positive_example: three boxes, two cities, five books

l1_notes.uz: MUHIM: o'zbekchada sondan keyin ko'plik qo'shilmaydi ('besh kitob'), ingliz tilida esa SHART ('five books').
l1_notes.ru: После числительных в английском всегда множественное число.

can_do: I can make plurals correctly and say them.

label: irregular plurals
form: man→men, woman→women, child→children, person→people, foot→feet, tooth→teeth, mouse→mice, fish→fish, sheep→sheep

explanation.en: These nouns do not take -s. Learn them as pairs.
explanation.uz: Bu otlar -s olmaydi. Juftlik sifatida yodlang.

positive_example: There are three children in the room.
negative_example: There are three childs in the room.

l1_notes.uz: 'people' — ko'plik: 'people are', 'people is' emas. 'woman' /ˈwʊmən/ va 'women' /ˈwɪmɪn/ talaffuzi butunlay farq qiladi.

can_do: I can use the common irregular plurals.

label: a / an
form: a + consonant sound; an + vowel sound

explanation.en: Use a or an the first time you mention a singular countable thing. It depends on the SOUND, not the letter: an hour, a university.
explanation.uz: Birlikdagi sanaladigan otni birinchi marta aytganda a/an ishlatiladi. TOVUSHGA qarab tanlanadi: an hour, a university.

positive_example: She's a doctor. I have an idea.
negative_example: She's doctor. I have a idea.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek va rus tillarida artikl YO'Q — bu eng uzoq davom etadigan qiyinchilik. Kasb aytilganda artikl SHART: 'I am a teacher'.

can_do: I can use a and an correctly.

label: the
form: the + singular, plural or uncountable noun

explanation.en: Use the when both people know which one: the sun, the door, and the second time you mention something.
explanation.uz: Ikkala tomon qaysi biri ekanini bilsa 'the' ishlatiladi: the sun, the door, hamda ikkinchi marta eslatilganda.

positive_example: I saw a dog. The dog was very big.
negative_example: I saw a dog. A dog was very big.

l1_notes.uz: Artikl yo'qligi sababli 'the' ni ham tushirib qo'yish, ham ortiqcha ishlatish uchraydi. Qoida: birinchi marta → a/an, ikkinchi marta → the.

can_do: I can use the when we both know which thing I mean.

label: zero article
form: no article before plurals and uncountables in general statements; meals, languages, most countries

explanation.en: Use no article for things in general: I like music. I speak English. We have lunch at one.
explanation.uz: Umumiy ma'noda artikl ishlatilmaydi: I like music. I speak English. We have lunch at one.

negative_example: I like the coffee. (meaning coffee in general)

l1_notes.uz: Bu holat o'zbek tiliga eng yaqin — artikl umuman yo'q. Qiyinchilik 'the' ni ortiqcha qo'shishda.

can_do: I can talk about things in general without an article.

label: this / that / these / those
form: this (sing, near), that (sing, far), these (pl, near), those (pl, far)

explanation.en: This and these are near. That and those are far. These and those are plural.
explanation.uz: this/these — yaqin. that/those — uzoq. these/those — ko'plik.

positive_example: What are these? — These are pens.

l1_notes.uz: 'bu/bular', 'u/ular' — o'zbekchada ham bor, bu oson. Faqat fe'lning son bo'yicha mosligini unutmang.

can_do: I can point at things and name them.

label: countable and uncountable nouns — first set
form: water, bread, money, information, advice, news, furniture, luggage, work, rice, sugar, tea, coffee, music, time
meaning: things we cannot count one by one

explanation.en: Uncountable nouns have no plural and take no a/an: some water, not a water.
explanation.uz: Sanalmaydigan otlarda ko'plik ham, a/an ham bo'lmaydi: some water, 'a water' emas.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada bu otlar sanalishi mumkin ('bir maslahat'), ingliz tilida esa yo'q: 'a piece of advice'.

can_do: I can use uncountable nouns like water and advice correctly.

label: some / any
form: some in affirmatives and offers; any in negatives and questions

explanation.en: Some in positive sentences and offers; any in negatives and most questions.
explanation.uz: Some — tasdiqda va taklifda; any — inkorda va aksariyat savollarda.

positive_example: I've got some bread, but I haven't got any butter.

l1_notes.uz: 'some/any' ning o'zbekchada aniq ekvivalenti yo'q — gap turiga qarab tanlang.

can_do: I can talk about quantities in shops and at home.

label: a lot of / lots of / much / many / a little / a few
form: much + uncountable; many + countable; a lot of + both

explanation.en: Many counts (many books); much does not (much water). A lot of works with both.
explanation.uz: many — sanaladiganlar bilan (many books); much — sanalmaydiganlar bilan (much water). a lot of — ikkalasi bilan.

positive_example: There isn't much time, but there are a lot of people.

l1_notes.uz: much/many farqi o'zbekchada yo'q ('ko'p' hamma joyda) — sanaladimi yoki yo'qmi, avval shuni aniqlang.

can_do: I can say how much or how many of something there is.

label: How much…? / How many…?
form: How much + uncountable; How many + countable

explanation.en: How many for things you can count; how much for things you cannot — and for prices.
explanation.uz: How many — sanaladiganlar uchun; how much — sanalmaydiganlar va narx uchun.

positive_example: How much is this? How many brothers do you have?

l1_notes.uz: Narx so'raganda doim 'How much…?'.

can_do: I can ask prices and quantities in a shop.

label: subject pronouns
form: I, you, he, she, it, we, they

explanation.en: English always needs a subject. I is always a capital letter.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tilida ega DOIM kerak. 'I' har doim katta harf bilan yoziladi.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada ega tushib qolishi mumkin ('Keldim'), ingliz tilida esa mumkin emas. 'u' jinssiz — he/she ni to'g'ri tanlang.

can_do: I can use he, she and it correctly.

label: object pronouns
form: me, you, him, her, it, us, them

explanation.en: Use these after a verb or a preposition: I like him. Come with me.
explanation.uz: Fe'ldan yoki predlogdan keyin ishlatiladi: I like him. Come with me.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada to'ldiruvchi tushib qolishi mumkin ('Yoqtiraman'); ingliz tilida 'it' ni qo'shish shart: 'I like it'.

can_do: I can use me, him, her and them correctly.

label: impersonal it
form: It is + weather / time / distance
use: talking about weather, time and distance

explanation.en: English needs a subject even when there is no real one: It's cold. It's five o'clock.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tilida haqiqiy ega bo'lmasa ham 'it' qo'yiladi: It's cold. It's five o'clock.

known_errors: *Today is cold. (acceptable but It's cold today is more natural)

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada 'sovuq' yetarli; ingliz tilida esa ega majburiy.

can_do: I can talk about the time and the weather.

label: one / ones
form: one (singular), ones (plural) replacing a known noun

explanation.en: Use one or ones instead of repeating the noun: I'll take the red one.
explanation.uz: Otni takrorlamaslik uchun: I'll take the red one.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada sifat o'zi yetarli ('ko'kini'); ingliz tilida 'one' qo'shiladi.

can_do: I can choose between things in a shop.

label: adjective position
form: adjective + noun; be + adjective; adjectives never take -s

explanation.en: Adjectives go before the noun or after be. They never take -s.
explanation.uz: Sifat otdan OLDIN yoki 'be' dan KEYIN keladi. Sifatga hech qachon -s qo'shilmaydi.

negative_example: They are talls boys. / They are boys tall.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada ham sifat otdan oldin keladi — bu oson. Faqat sifat ko'plik olmasligini eslang.

can_do: I can describe things with adjectives.

label: adjective order — first set
form: opinion + size + colour + noun
meaning: the fixed order of multiple adjectives

explanation.en: When you use more than one adjective, the order is: opinion, size, colour. A nice big red car.
explanation.uz: Bir nechta sifat bo'lsa tartib: fikr, o'lcham, rang. A nice big red car.

l1_notes.uz: Bu tartibni ona tilida so'zlashuvchilar sezib turadi — mashq bilan avtomatlashadi.

can_do: I can use two or three adjectives in the right order.

label: very / really / quite / too + adjective
form: intensifier + adjective

explanation.en: Very and really make an adjective stronger. Too means more than you want — it is negative.
explanation.uz: very va really sifatni kuchaytiradi. 'too' esa 'keragidan ortiq' degani — salbiy ma'no.

positive_example: This coffee is too hot. I can't drink it.
negative_example: This coffee is too good. (meaning: very good)

l1_notes.uz: 'too' = 'juda' EMAS, 'keragidan ortiq'. 'juda' → 'very'. Bu juda ko'p uchraydigan xato.

can_do: I can make my descriptions stronger.

label: comparative adjectives
form: short adj + -er + than; long adj: more + adj + than

explanation.en: One syllable: add -er. Three or more syllables: use more. Two syllables: -y becomes -ier.
explanation.uz: Bir bo'g'in: -er. Uch va undan ko'p bo'g'in: more. Ikki bo'g'inli -y bilan tugasa: -ier.

negative_example: Samarkand is more old than Tashkent.

l1_notes.uz: '-roq' qo'shimchasi kabi. Ikki marta qiyoslamang: 'more bigger' noto'g'ri.

can_do: I can compare two things.

label: superlative adjectives
form: the + adj + -est; the most + adj
use: talking about the best, biggest, most famous

explanation.en: Superlatives always take the: the biggest, the most beautiful.
explanation.uz: Orttirma daraja doim 'the' bilan keladi: the biggest, the most beautiful.

positive_example: It's the biggest city in Uzbekistan.

l1_notes.uz: 'eng' — lekin ingliz tilida 'the' ni unutmang.

can_do: I can say which is the biggest or the best.

label: irregular comparison
form: good/better/best, bad/worse/worst, far/further/furthest, much-many/more/most, little/less/least

explanation.en: These five do not follow the rules. Learn them as sets of three.
explanation.uz: Bu beshtasi qoidaga bo'ysunmaydi. Uchtalik guruh sifatida yodlang.

positive_example: This one is better, but that one is the best.

l1_notes.uz: 'yaxshi/yaxshiroq/eng yaxshi' — ingliz tilida butunlay boshqa so'zlar.

can_do: I can use better, best, worse and worst.

label: as … as
form: as + adjective + as; not as … as
meaning: says two things are equal or not equal

explanation.en: As … as means the same. Not as … as means less.
explanation.uz: as … as — teng. not as … as — kamroq.

positive_example: Bukhara is not as big as Tashkent.
negative_example: Bukhara is not so big than Tashkent.
known_errors: *not so big as (acceptable but less common)

l1_notes.uz: '-day/-dek' kabi. Sifat asl shaklda qoladi, -er QO'SHILMAYDI.

can_do: I can say two things are the same or not the same.

label: prepositions of time — at / on / in
form: at + clock time and night; on + days and dates; in + months, years, seasons, parts of the day

explanation.en: at a point (at 6, at night), on a day (on Monday), in a longer period (in May, in the morning).
explanation.uz: at — nuqta (at 6, at night); on — kun (on Monday); in — uzunroq davr (in May, in the morning).

positive_example: I start work at nine on Monday.
negative_example: I start work in nine in Monday.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada kelishik qo'shimchasi ('-da') hamma holatda bir xil — ingliz tilida esa uchta har xil predlog. Ularni ibora sifatida yodlang.

can_do: I can say when something happens.

label: prepositions of place
form: in, on, at, under, behind, in front of, next to, between, opposite, near, above, below

explanation.en: in = inside; on = touching a surface; at = a point or place.
explanation.uz: in = ichida; on = yuzasida; at = nuqta yoki joy.

positive_example: The book is on the table, next to the lamp.
negative_example: The book is in the table.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekcha '-da' uchun in/on/at dan bittasini tanlash kerak — otga qarab yodlang: 'in the picture', 'on the bus', 'at home'.

can_do: I can say where things are.

label: prepositions of movement
form: to, from, into, out of, up, down, along, across, through

explanation.en: Use to for a destination: I go to school. Never say to home.
explanation.uz: Manzil uchun 'to': I go to school. Lekin 'to home' DEYILMAYDI — faqat 'go home'.

positive_example: Go along this street and across the bridge.
negative_example: Go in this street and cross of the bridge.

l1_notes.uz: 'uyga bormoq' → 'go home' (to YO'Q). 'arrive' bilan 'to' emas, 'at/in' ishlatiladi.

can_do: I can give and follow simple directions.

label: fixed place phrases
form: at home, at work, at school, in bed, on holiday, at the moment
meaning: common place expressions with no article

explanation.en: These phrases have no article. Learn them as whole units.
explanation.uz: Bu iboralarda artikl yo'q. Ularni yaxlit holda yodlang.

l1_notes.uz: Bu iboralarni grammatika emas, lug'at sifatida yodlang.

can_do: I can say where I am using common phrases.

label: basic word order (SVO)
form: Subject + Verb + Object (+ place) (+ time)
meaning: the fixed order of an English sentence

explanation.en: English word order is fixed: who — does what — to what. The object comes straight after the verb.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tilida so'z tartibi QAT'IY: kim — nima qiladi — nimani. To'ldiruvchi fe'ldan darhol keyin keladi.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekcha SOV (fe'l oxirida), ingliz tili SVO (fe'l o'rtada). Bu eng chuqur farq — har bir gapda tekshiring.
l1_notes.ru: Русский порядок слов свободный; английский — фиксированный.

can_do: I can build a correct English sentence.

label: coordination — and, but, or, so, because
form: clause + conjunction + clause

explanation.en: and adds, but contrasts, or gives a choice, so gives a result, because gives a reason.
explanation.uz: and — qo'shadi, but — qarama-qarshi qo'yadi, or — tanlov, so — natija, because — sabab.

positive_example: I like tea, but I don't like coffee.
negative_example: Although I like tea, but I don't like coffee.
known_errors: *I like tea, I don't like coffee. (no conjunction)

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada 'garchi … lekin' juft ishlatiladi; ingliz tilida faqat BITTASI bo'lishi kerak.

can_do: I can join two ideas in one sentence.

label: question words
form: what, where, when, who, why, how, how much, how many, how old, how often, which, whose
meaning: asks for different kinds of information

explanation.en: Choose the question word by what you want to know: what (thing), where (place), when (time), who (person), why (reason), how (manner).
explanation.uz: Nimani bilmoqchi bo'lsangiz, shunga qarab so'roq so'zini tanlang: what (narsa), where (joy), when (vaqt), who (odam), why (sabab), how (qanday).

l1_notes.uz: 'Necha yoshdasiz?' → 'How old are you?' — 'How many years…' EMAS. Yosh 'be' bilan aytiladi: 'I am 20', 'I have 20' emas.

can_do: I can ask all the basic question types.
